# 2 Baruch Chapter 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**1** I went out and settled in a cave in the Kidron valley, and I fasted there for seven days.

**2** After seven days, I looked up toward heaven and began to pray:

**3** O Lord my God — you who called the very beginning into existence before the ages began, you who hold the passing of all time in your hands —

**4** Your throne stands in heights beyond all reckoning, and your glory stretches beyond anything that can be fathomed.

**5** The armies of angels stand trembling before you, serving in fear and fire before your presence.

**6** You have no beginning and no end. You have sustained the living by your word and called forth the dead by your command.

**7** You have set the number of the living and fixed the boundaries for the dead. No king can overstep your decrees.

**8** You remember everything; nothing that has ever been created escapes your memory.

**9** Hear my prayer, O Lord. Pay attention to my cry.

**10** For all of us together are nothing in your sight — we are as if we never existed at all, like a single drop in a vast bucket.

**11** We vanish like morning mist; our strength is nothing but vapor.

**12** Our days are measured by your goodness; our years are counted by the compassion of your hand.

**13** For the Most High is great, and the Mighty One is powerful — and he has not forgotten a single human being.

**14** O Lord, you have heard the prayers of those who have already died, and the departed stand in awe of you.

**15** Was it not written long ago by the prophets: The days are coming when the Most High will come to reckon with the world he made?

**16** He will call to account those who broke his commandments. He will judge the living through the testimony of the dead, and he will repay the transgressors with the full fruit of what they have done.

**17** He will wake those who sleep in the dust. He will bring out those living ones who have been waiting for him. He will usher into the heavenly treasury those who have been sealed, to take their rest at last.

**18** Then he will destroy those who corrupted themselves, and hand over those who defiled themselves to the fire.

**19** And when he has brought all corruption to its end, renewed the age, and awakened those who slept in hope of him —

**20** Then at last his rest will come.

**21** You alone can do all of this, O Lord — and so I speak these words before you.

**22** Your furnace is full and ready. Yet your compassion is being held back from the people who live today.

**23** If only you had compassion on those who are alive right now — if you would speed up your timetable and cut short the measure of the ages —

**24** Your treasury would not have been left waiting, and the age to come would not have been delayed so long.

**25** Great is your strength, O Lord; great is your glory; great is your beauty; great is your grace; great is your compassion. Amen and amen.

**26** After praying, I remained in that place for another seven days.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering of Baruch's great prayer in ch. 21. The prayer sweeps through God's eternal attributes — his sovereignty over time, the dead, and the coming age — before making the bold plea that God would hasten the end for the sake of the living.*
